title: Paid far above the national norm for the same service
question: Which San Francisco providers were paid much more than providers anywhere else in the country for the same service in the same year?
finding: 20 San Francisco provider numbers (13 of them outside City government and the University of California) were paid more than 99 in 100 billers nationwide for a service while also getting at least three times the national median per claim line and half as much again as other California billers: 126 service-years and $1,076 million in all, $32.0 million of it to the 13 others.
how: For every provider, service code and year the total paid was set against the national 99th percentile for that code and year, and the amount per claim line against the median across all billers in the country. A row needs the total above the 99th percentile, at least three times the national median per line, at least one and a half times what other California billers averaged per line for the same service (rates are set State by State), 100 claim lines, $100,000 and 50 billers nationwide. For a service with only 15 to 49 billers in the country the bar is $1 million, the largest total in the country and a quarter of everything California paid for it, with other California billers to compare against. Each provider is shown once, on its largest such service-year; private providers come first, ranked by the multiple.
limits: An outlier is a reason to look, not a finding. A claim line can carry many units: California counties bill mental health by the minute, so one line can be a whole session, and public clinics and City ambulances are paid cost-based rates set by the State. A specialty explains many gaps. Health-plan payments are reported differently from direct State payments. Cells under 12 claims are withheld and 2024 is preliminary. The address is where the provider is registered, not where the patient was seen.
